messages.subject: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table
messages.subject_clean: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nimble Users,

I'm working on building a model where one of the parameters (I'm calling it R) is a deterministic function of other model parameters, but this function requires numerical integration.  Since we can't call out to other R packages to do the numerical integration in a nimble function yet, I was thinking of creating a lookup table for R instead.  However, I understand that indexing via R's boolean vectors (e.g. x[x>5]) is not accessible in the Nimble language.  Do you have any ideas how I might write a Nimble function to use a lookup table?

An Example Lookup Table:
R   param1  param2
3         1            1
4         1            2
...

So I want something like:
"lookupR(1,1)" returns "table[ table[,2]==1 & table[,3]==1 , 1 ]"

messages.body_plain:
Your welcome :0)

How about the following for the round problem. "as.integer" and "sign" were both problematic.

roundNim <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0) ){
      returnType(double(0))
      absx <- abs(x)
      low  <- floor(absx)   ## as.integer(absx)
      high <- ceiling(absx) ## as.integer(absx + 1)

      if ( (absx-low) < 0.50 ){

          out <- low * (-1)^(x < 0)
      } else {
          out <- high * (-1)^(x < 0)
      }
      return(out)
  }
)

c_roundNim <- compileNimble(roundNim)

c_roundNim(0.56)  ## 1
c_roundNim(0.46)  ## 0
c_roundNim(-0.56) ## -1
c_roundNim(-0.46) ## 0

c_roundNim(1.5)  ## 2
c_roundNim(0.5)  ## 1
c_roundNim(-0.5) ## -1
c_roundNim(-1.5) ## -2

f = nimbleFunction(run=function(x = double(0)) {

return(y)
})

messages.body_plain:
Following Daniel’s response: Are you using a version that shows the progress bar, and if so is that adequate to your need?

We’ve had some delays updating versions due to CRAN issues.  If you install from CRAN or from our development branch (“devel”) in GitHub, you’ll get the progress bars.  To do the latter, you can use

library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")

If you want something more than the progress bar, you could go into the package source code, into file MCMC_build.R, copy the buildMCMC nimbleFunction into your own code file with changes in the run function to output what you want, and use that version instead of buildMCMC.  You might need to remove the “where = getLoadingNamespace()” as that is particular to nimbleFunctions when defined in package source code. Let me know if that doesn’t make sense.

Perry

messages.subject: Codes not compiling after installing new nimble version
messages.subject_clean: Codes not compiling after installing new nimble version
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I created a simple multivariate model for learning Nimble. It was running fine earlier (when I had installed nimble as is mentioned in the nimble website). Now I have reinstalled nimble from

library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")

to get the progressBar option. But now the code is no longer compiling. I tried other multivariate codes that I created and none of them are compiling.

Here is the code:

multiCode <- nimbleCode({
  mu[] <- theta*rep(1,SAMPLES)
  V[,] <- sigma *diag(SAMPLES)
  y[] ~ dmnorm(mu[], cholesky = V[,], prec_param=0);
  theta ~ dnorm(0,sd=100)
  sigma ~ dunif(0, 100)
})

multiModel <- nimbleModel(multiCode, constants = list(SAMPLES = SAMPLES), dimensions=list(y=SAMPLES, mu=SAMPLES, V=c(SAMPLES, SAMPLES)), check=FALSE)

set.seed(1)
SAMPLES=1000
data <- rnorm(SAMPLES,-3,5)

multiModel$setData(list(y = data))

multiModel$sigma <- 20
multiModel$theta <- 4

compiled_multiModel <- compileNimble(multiModel)

multiMCMC <- buildMCMC(multiModel)

CmultiMCMC <- compileNimble(multiMCMC, project = multiModel)

CmultiMCMC$run(10000)

Here are the errors that I get:

> compiled_multiModel <- compileNimble(multiModel)
compiling... this may take a minute. Use nimbleOptions(showCompilerOutput = TRUE) to see C++ compiler details.
Error: Failed to create the shared library

> multiMCMC <- buildMCMC(multiModel)

> CmultiMCMC <- compileNimble(multiMCMC, project = multiModel)
compiling... this may take a minute. Use nimbleOptions(showCompilerOutput = TRUE) to see C++ compiler details.
Error in Robject[[fxnVecName]]$model$CobjectInterface$.nodeFxnPointers_byDeclID :
  $ operator not defined for this S4 class

messages.body_plain:
I suspect the issue is that rep() and diag() are not supported in BUGS code.  It is possible that in an earlier version of nimble they worked “by accident” due to partial evaluation of constant expressions from R.  Can you try setting mu[] and V[,] more directly from a constant set up from R?

Perry

messages.body_plain:
Hi Abhirup, in this case it is best to define mu as a constant and V
as sigma times a constant identity matrix. Then set the values of mu
and of the identity matrix _outside_ of the BUGS code so that NIMBLE
doesn't create a node for each element of the mu and identity matrix
variables. Creating all those nodes is probably what is taking so long
(presumably SAMPLES is quite large -- we've done a lot in the last few
months to reduce model building time so it should only take a while if
SAMPLES is large).

e.g., in BUGS code, take out all the lines that initialize mu and V
and instead have:
V[,] <- sigma * identity[,]
y[] ~ dmnorm(mu[],cholesky = V[,], prec_param=0)

then when you pass in constants to nimbleModel, set:
constants = list(mu = rep(0, SAMPLES), identity = diag(rep(1,
SAMPLES)), SAMPLES=SAMPLES)
